name: Subhas Chandra Bose
role: Indian nationalist leader; Congress president (1938-39), founder of the Forward Bloc, head of the Provisional Government of Azad Hind and the Indian National Army (1943-45)
summary: Bose was a left-wing nationalist who demanded complete independence, a Socialist Republic with state ownership and national planning, and the end of caste and communal divisions. After leaving the Congress he turned to armed struggle, allying with Germany, Italy and Japan to fight Britain. He said India should find its own path, which in 1934 he called a synthesis of communism and fascism.

sources.title: The Indian Struggle, 1920-1942 (Netaji: Collected Works, Vol. 2)
sources.author: Subhas Chandra Bose

sources.title: Bose, Subhas Chandra
sources.author: Banglapedia: National Encyclopedia of Bangladesh
sources.usedFor: Career summary: Congress presidency, Forward Bloc, Axis support, INA and Provisional Government.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He held that poverty and scientific production and distribution can be tackled 'only along socialistic lines' with state ownership and planning (Haripura presidential address (Feb 1938), in Selected Speeches).

public-ownership.rationale: In the Haripura presidential address (Feb 1938), in Selected Speeches he calls for a comprehensive scheme of industrial development under State ownership and State control, and at the 1938 National Planning Committee he wants power, machinery, metals, chemicals and railways controlled by the State.

unions-good.rationale: Presiding over the All-India Trade Union Congress in 1931 he said the trade union movement is destined to grow, defended workers' right to work and a living wage, and wanted unions free of employer victimisation.

property-fundamental.rationale: He called for abolishing landlordism and gradually socialising agriculture and industry (Haripura presidential address (Feb 1938), in Selected Speeches), which treats property as overridable.

decide-locally.rationale: At Haripura he wanted a strong central government to unify India against invasion, while granting provinces and minorities a large measure of governmental and cultural autonomy and a federal republic with willing States.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: In his 1928 Poona and 1929 Rangpur addresses he defended Indian culture and its continuity against Western criticism, and the Congress policy he restates protects cultural diversity.

gradual-change.rationale: At Karachi in 1931 he attacked the Congress for a programme of 'adjustments' between landlord and tenant, capitalist and wage earner, rather than radicalism, and called for revolutionary change.

revolution-justified.rationale: As head of the Provisional Government of Azad Hind (1943-45) he raised the Indian National Army and declared war on Britain, and in Singapore (4 July 1943) declared that 'the time to start an armed struggle for freedom has come'.

central-planning.rationale: The Haripura presidential address (Feb 1938), in Selected Speeches says the State, advised by a Planning Commission, should gradually socialise the whole agricultural and industrial system in production and distribution; The Indian Struggle also counts state planning among communism's real contributions.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He wanted a Planning Commission to set the direction of industry; his 1938 planning speech names the 'mother industries' (power, metals, heavy chemicals, machinery, transport) the State should develop first.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Indian Struggle (1934) lists party dictatorship among the common traits of the communism-fascism synthesis he expected; at Haripura (1938) he wanted the winning party to hold power but said other parties should not be banned and the party must be democratic.

democracy-best.rationale: He called democracy a human institution and wanted political democracy built on a democratic society (1928), yet in 1934 predicted a synthesis in which parliamentary democracy is denounced; he stressed the party's democratic basis in 1938.

political-violence-never.rationale: His record from 1943 to 1945 is armed struggle: he founded the Provisional Government, took direct command of the INA and led it into India; his earlier Congress years used non-violent methods but he never held violence to be never justified.

separate-church-state.rationale: He restates the Congress commitment that the State shall observe neutrality in regard to all religions and not interfere in religion or culture; this is neutrality rather than a strict-separation doctrine (Haripura presidential address (Feb 1938), in Selected Speeches).

equal-outcomes.rationale: His 1929 definition of freedom includes equal distribution of wealth alongside equal opportunities regardless of caste, creed or religion (Poona 1928 and Lahore 1929 addresses).

limit-population.rationale: The Haripura presidential address (Feb 1938), in Selected Speeches says it is desirable to restrict population until the existing people can be fed, clothed and educated, and urges public attention to the question (methods left open).

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The Haripura presidential address (Feb 1938), in Selected Speeches says that however much one dislikes modern industrialism 'we cannot go back to the pre-industrial era' and that India should reconcile itself to industrialisation while keeping cottage industries where viable.

return-to-foraging.rationale: He accepted industrialisation as unavoidable and rejected going back to a pre-industrial era (Haripura presidential address (Feb 1938), in Selected Speeches).

collective-farming.rationale: He proposed gradually socialising agriculture in both production and distribution and extending the cooperative movement, but did not spell out collective farming (Haripura presidential address (Feb 1938), in Selected Speeches).

national-rebirth.rationale: His Lahore address of 1929 says old and worn-out civilisations are rejuvenated only through revolution and calls for a revolution of ideas to create a new, progressive nation.

national-self-determination.rationale: He demanded complete independence and 'real self-determination' for India, rejected Dominion status, and welcomed independence for Burma and the Philippines (Haripura 1938; Singapore 1943).

dominated-front.rationale: He attended the Greater East Asia Conference in Tokyo (Nov 1943) as head of the Provisional Government and called Japan the first Asiatic nation to stand up to the Western powers, urging Asian nations' common cause against Anglo-American imperialism.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: In his Haripura address he restates the Congress fundamental rights that all citizens are equal before the law irrespective of religion, caste, creed or sex.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: In the Haripura presidential address (Feb 1938), in Selected Speeches he affirms the Congress position that no interference in religion or culture is intended and that a minority is entitled to keep its personal law without change imposed by the majority.

minority-language-support.rationale: He restates the Congress policy that the culture, language and script of minorities and linguistic areas shall be protected, and promises minorities large cultural autonomy (Haripura presidential address (Feb 1938), in Selected Speeches).

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: At Lahore in 1929 he defined freedom as including not only release from political bondage but also equal distribution of wealth and abolition of caste barriers; at Karachi in 1931 he called for a Socialist Republic.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Haripura presidential address (Feb 1938), in Selected Speeches says eradicating poverty requires radical reform of the land system, including the abolition of landlordism, and cheap credit and cooperatives for the rural population.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: In his 1928 Poona address he says privileges based on birth, caste or creed should go, and in 1931 he called for abolition of the caste system.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He fought British rule as enslavement and called British imperialism India's one enemy; he never accepted that one people may rule another for its improvement (broadcast of 1 May 1942).

party-own-road.rationale: Presiding at the 1931 Trade Union Congress he said India should evolve her own form of socialism and her own methods, since 'you can never rule out geography or history'.

religious-nation.rationale: He repeatedly defines the nation across communities (Poona 1928: unity through cultural rapprochement; INA 1943: Indians united regardless of religion or caste).

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Indian Struggle (1934) argued the next phase would be a synthesis of communism and fascism, not a choice between them; in 1939 he said he meant socialism after freedom and that the expression was unhappy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He condemned British rule as a system of exploitation: the British aristocracy and bourgeoisie 'exist primarily because there are colonies and dependencies to exploit' and he fought it (Haripura presidential address (Feb 1938), in Selected Speeches).

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: In 1941-43 he sought alliance with Germany, Italy and Japan; the Provisional Government he headed declared war on Britain and the United States and fought beside Japan.

uniformed-youth.rationale: At Karachi in 1931 he called for organising youth into Volunteer Corps under strict discipline, and in Bengal he built the Congress volunteer corps; the sources do not describe uniforms and drill in detail.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: His Provisional Government renamed the Andaman Islands 'Shaheed' (martyr) in memory of India's martyrs, and he called Bhagat Singh a symbol of the spirit of revolt and Kasturba Gandhi a martyr.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Replying to the Bombay Corporation in 1938 he praised 'municipal socialism', the collective effort of municipalities as in Vienna and Birmingham, to serve the whole community.

communal-electorates.rationale: He repeats that the Congress opposes the Communal Decision (separate electorates) as anti-national and anti-democratic and a barrier to Indian unity; The Indian Struggle also treats it as a British divide-and-rule device.

women-suffrage.rationale: He restates the Congress policy of universal adult suffrage and no disability for office by reason of sex, and in 1928 said women's status should be raised and women trained for public affairs (Haripura presidential address (Feb 1938), in Selected Speeches; Poona 1928).

no-denominational-politics.rationale: At Lahore in 1929 he lists destruction of communalism and religious intolerance as part of freedom, and in 1928 argued economic education would stop masses being 'pawns in communal feuds'.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: At Poona in 1928 he pleaded for a coalition between labour (including peasants) and nationalism, and rejected international Communism's attack on nationalism.

small-step-social-reform.rationale: His 1931 Karachi address rejects a programme of adjustments and calls for organising peasants and workers on a socialistic programme and abolishing caste, not reform by small steps.

colonial-socialism-democratic-stage.rationale: At Poona in 1928 he said that before India can be rebuilt on a socialistic or other new basis it must first win the right to shape its own destiny, so political independence comes first.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: He led armed resistance against British rule (INA, 1943-45), which he described as rule held by the sword; British colonial rule is a related rather than identical case to military occupation.

notes: Over time: Congress years (1921-40) used non-violent methods and he stated at Haripura (1938) that satyagraha should remain the method; from 1941 to 1945 he worked for armed struggle with Axis help, kept in words and acts for four years, so violence and bloc answers follow that record. His 1934 praise of a communism-fascism synthesis was clarified in 1939. Themes searched: economy, land, labour, society and religion, government and party, foreign alliances, women, language. Searched his own texts for law and order, criminal justice, environment, technology, gender and family, money and trade and found no stated position, so those are null. The Selected Speeches volume was read through keyword searches, not cover to cover. Borrowable books (Netaji Collected Works volumes 5, 9, 10, 11, 12 and Crossroads) were not accessible.
